name: Espressif ESP32-C3-MINI-1-H4X module (PCB antenna, 4 MB flash)
description: Certified 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11 b/g/n) and Bluetooth 5 LE module on the ESP32-C3FH4X (32-bit RISC-V single core up to 160 MHz, 400 KB SRAM, chip revision v1.1) with 4 MB in-package Quad SPI flash, 40 MHz crystal and PCB antenna. 53 pins: 15 GPIO (ADC on GPIO0-5, UART0, USB Serial/JTAG on GPIO18/19, JTAG), EN, 3V3. Supply 3.0-3.6 V, at least 0.5 A. -40 to 105 °C. 13.2 x 16.6 x 2.4 mm.

params.note: VDD33 3.0-3.6 V (typ 3.3 V); the external supply must deliver at least 0.5 A. Absolute maximum 3.6 V. Figure 9-1 places 10 uF and 0.1 uF on VDD33; R1/C3 (values left to be determined in the figure) form the EN RC delay. The module has an ESD diode on VDD33. The rails must be stable at least 50 us before EN rises.

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

GPIO2 is a strapping pin, latched at chip reset (hold time >= 3 ms after CHIP_EN rises). It does not select SPI or download boot, but a pull-up is recommended because of glitches (floating by default).

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

params.description: High: on, enables the chip. Low: off, the chip powers off. Note: Do not leave the EN pin floating.

params.note: CHIP_EN has no pull-up inside the module. Espressif recommends an RC delay at EN, usually R = 10 kOhm and C = 1 uF, adjusted to the supply's power-up timing. Hold EN below VIL_nRST (0.25 x VDD) for at least 50 us to reset; it releases above VIH_nRST (0.75 x VDD). EN low: power off, 1 uA.

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

RTC IO (powered by VDD3P3_RTC): can wake the chip from Deep-sleep (esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup) and can hold its level in Deep-sleep. GPIO6-21 are high impedance in Deep-sleep and wake it only from Light-sleep.

ADC2 has one channel and is not factory-calibrated. Errata ADC-183 (affects v0.0-v1.1, so this v1.1 module): the DMA digital controller of SAR ADC2 cannot work; Espressif suggests SAR ADC1. Use GPIO0-4 (ADC1) for continuous/DMA sampling.

GPIO8 is a strapping pin, latched at chip reset (hold time >= 3 ms after CHIP_EN rises). Floating by default. Joint download boot needs GPIO8 = 1 (with GPIO9 = 0); with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL it also gates ROM messages on UART0.
GPIO9 is a strapping pin, latched at chip reset (hold time >= 3 ms after CHIP_EN rises). Weak internal pull-up (1 = SPI boot). Pull it low at reset for joint download boot (UART0 or USB Serial/JTAG).

USB Serial/JTAG (USB 2.0 full speed, 12 Mbit/s) is only available on GPIO18/GPIO19; USB_D- and USB_D+ can be swapped in a register (USB_SERIAL_JTAG_EXCHG_PINS). The USB function is enabled by default, with the USB pull-up on GPIO19; disabled, the pins are plain GPIO with their pulls off.

USB Serial/JTAG (USB 2.0 full speed, 12 Mbit/s) is only available on GPIO18/GPIO19; USB_D- and USB_D+ can be swapped in a register (USB_SERIAL_JTAG_EXCHG_PINS). The USB function is enabled by default, with the USB pull-up on GPIO19; disabled, the pins are plain GPIO with their pulls off.
The module puts a 499 Ohm resistor in series with U0TXD (module schematic R2).

Centre ground pad (EPAD in the module schematic), 3 x 3 squares of 1.45 mm, 5.4 mm overall. Soldering it to base-board ground is not a must, but improves thermal performance; too much paste can lift the module and weaken the other joints.

interfaces.name: UART0 (U0RXD GPIO20 pin 30 / U0TXD GPIO21 pin 31)

profiles.label: UART0 (U0RXD GPIO20 pin 30 / U0TXD GPIO21 pin 31)

params.note: UART0 is the firmware download and log port (joint download boot, ROM messages). UART controllers run up to 5 Mbps with hardware (RTS/CTS) and software flow control; UART0's signals can also be moved to other GPIO through the GPIO matrix, but download boot uses these pins.

CDC-ACM virtual serial port and JTAG adapter with an integrated full-speed PHY: flashes the in-package flash and debugs the CPU over USB with no bridge chip. The module has no VBUS pin; the controller runs from 3V3. Joint download boot works over USB Serial/JTAG as well as UART0.

interfaces.name: JTAG (MTMS GPIO4, MTDI GPIO5, MTCK GPIO6, MTDO GPIO7)

params.note: Pad JTAG on GPIO4-7 (Table 3-1). The same pins are FSPIHD/FSPIWP/FSPICLK/FSPID and GPIO; USB Serial/JTAG gives JTAG without them.

params.standard: IEEE 802.11 b/g/n, 20/40 MHz, 1T1R up to 150 Mbps; Station, SoftAP, Station + SoftAP, promiscuous; 802.11mc FTM

params.note: PCB antenna at the module's short end. Place the module at the base-board edge with the antenna feed point close to the edge; overhang the antenna or cut the base board away under it, keep copper out of the antenna keep-out zone, and do not centre the module in a hollowed-out board. Keep at least 15 mm of clearance around the antenna inside the housing, and test throughput and range in the end product.
source: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-hardware-design-guidelines/en/latest/esp32c3/pcb-layout-design.html (General Principles of PCB Layout for Modules)

params.coexistence: internal Wi-Fi / Bluetooth co-existence sharing the same antenna

params.note: 53 pads on the module underside: 48 of 0.4 x 0.8 mm at 0.8 mm pitch, 4 corner pads 0.7 x 0.7 mm, and the 5.4 mm centre pad (pin 49). Module 13.2 x 16.6 x 2.4 mm (+-0.15). MSL 3; single reflow, peak 235-250 °C for 30-70 s, SAC305. Avoid ultrasonic cleaning or welding (crystal resonance).

params.power_up: VDD33 stable >= 50 us before CHIP_EN rises (tSTBL)

params.note: Boot: GPIO9 high at reset (default, weak pull-up) boots from flash; GPIO9 low with GPIO8 high enters joint download boot over UART0 or USB Serial/JTAG. A pull-up on GPIO2 is recommended. Strapping values are latched at reset; the pins are ordinary GPIO afterwards.

Peripheral pins are assigned in firmware through the GPIO matrix: I2C, SPI2, UART1, LED PWM, RMT, I2S and TWAI signals can use any GPIO. Espressif ranks GPIO2/8/9 (strapping), GPIO18/19 (USB), GPIO4-7 (JTAG) and GPIO20/21 (UART0) as usable with caution. Only GPIO0-5 have analog inputs and can wake from Deep-sleep.

params.field: shield offset from the pad-end edge
params.resolution: The dimensioned datasheet drawing is used for the generated shield; the STEP agrees with it on the shield size (11.95 x 9.95 mm) and its 0.62 mm offset from the right edge.

params.reason: The datasheet gives no single typical draw: it requires the external supply to deliver at least 0.5 A (Table 6-2), above the 350 mA Wi-Fi TX peak (Table 6-4). The requirement is used so a supply budget sizes the 3V3 source for RF bursts; average draw depends on the duty cycle (performance traits, power-domain metadata).

params.value: 3.0-3.6 V on every logic pad and EN
params.reason: The GPIO are powered from VDD33 (chip Table 2-1) and their levels are fractions of it (Table 6-3); the parameter states the VDD33 range so a 3.3 V rail checks against it.

params.value: pads at the STEP's centres and the drawing's sizes, 0.02 mm thick on the seating plane; antenna = top face of the antenna area
params.reason: The drawing dimensions pad sizes, pitch and field extents but not each pad centre or the plating thickness (the STEP uses 0.035 mm); the PCB antenna trace is not dimensioned, so its area of the PCB stands for it. The shield's Ø0.5 marking and the parts under the shield are not modelled.

params.note: Espressif links ESP32-C3-MINI-1_20210903_0.STEP from datasheet §11.1 and the modules page. No licence is stated, and the datasheet's notice grants no licence ('All rights reserved'), so it is not redistributed; it was used only to measure the pad centres and shield. Geometry generated from Figures 10-1 and 11-1 (library/cad/py/catalog/espressif-esp32-c3-mini-1-h4x.py).
No mass in the datasheet or on the modules page.

fields: ADC2 oneshot reads on chip revision v1.1
params.note: Errata ADC-183 lists v1.1 as affected: the DMA (digital) controller of SAR ADC2 cannot work. The errata says nothing about ADC2 oneshot reads, so whether GPIO5's ADC2_CH0 works in oneshot mode on v1.1 is not established; do not rely on it.
